transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 68 minutes
Location: All-Hands (virtual)
Attendees: Maya Kapoor (CEO), Ethan Park (CTO), Lila Ramos (VP Product), Daniel Kim (Head of Engineering), Jordan Blake (Head of Sales), Priya Singh (CFO), People Ops, All Employees

Summary:
Quick company update: Q4 review, hiring pause announcement, product roadmap for Q1, engineering reliability updates, questions from the team and holiday/ops notes.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Happy Friday, hope folks are caffeinated. We'll kick off with a quick set of updates then open for Q&A. I know everyone's heads down, so we'll try to be crisp.
[00:18] Ethan: quick note on infra — we've been seeing a 7% reduction in tail latency after the last kernel swap, so thank you infra team, that's real progress.
[00:32] Lila: product will show the Q1 roadmap briefly and call out a few pilot opportunities.
[00:40] Maya: culturally, we need to talk hiring. given the macro and our bookings comp, we're instituting a limited hiring pause for non-critical roles — product and infra hiring continues for key roles only. People Ops will share the policy after the call.
[01:02] Priya: to be clear on numbers — revenue came in 3% above plan for Q4, ARR growth is steady, but margins are tighter due to cloud costs and some benchmarking spend. We're prioritizing runway, so that's the context for the pause.
[01:25] Jordan: sales had a strong month with a couple of upsells into dedicated for two mid-market accounts; pipeline for Jan looks healthy. we'll share more in the GTM memo.
[01:40] Daniel: engineering — two notes, one is reliability work: we've tightened autoscaler thresholds which dropped error spikes during high concurrency tests. second, we started a KV cache migration for some legacy routes, ETA mid-Jan. small regressions possible, we'll notify CSE.
[02:02] Ethan: follow-up on kernel: the new path reduces memory copies for 8k sequences; it's promising but please flag any inference regressions, we rolled back a canary this week on a weird tokenization mismatch.
[02:27] Lila: roadmap slide — Q1 focus areas are: 1) Improve latency for long-context models, 2) Launch dedicated autoscaling policies, 3) Expand observability (token-level cost dashboards), 4) Integrations: KMS/HSM improvements for Private.
[02:56] Maya: big picture — we want predictable inference economics that customers can reason about. That means productizing some of the experimental knobs (batching profiles, quantization suggestions) so customers don't have to tune them themselves.
[03:20] Audience (q): are we open to pilot customers for the private on-prem package in EMEA?
[03:29] Lila: yes, selective pilots. legal and security have pre-approved some templates; we need SE and infra involvement. reach out to solutions-eng@ for intake.
[03:44] Maya: on partnerships — we've been talking to a cloud partner in APAC about region coverage, no signed deal yet, but it's promising for 2027 expansion.
[03:58] Priya: finance note — we're tightening vendor spend and negotiating reserved capacity discounts where it makes sense. please run purchases by procurement.
[04:12] Jordan: sales question — any change to discounting authority during hiring pause?
[04:18] Maya: not a change in policy; reps should continue to follow existing discount decks, but all large discounts need manager approval.
[04:30] Ethan: tech deep dive upcoming — we'll run two sessions in Jan: one on runtime optimizations (batching, kernel selection) and one on observability (tracing per route). engineers, please RSVP.
[04:50] Daniel: we also plan a canary rollout framework for model variants — automated fallback if latency/wrong outputs exceed thresholds. early tests show it works but need more coverage.
[05:10] Audience (q): will billing change for embeddings vs generation?
[05:17] Priya: no immediate billing changes, but we're exploring finer-grained unit economics to reflect cost differences across model types — if we change anything we'll announce early.
[05:34] Maya: OK let's go into a few highlights from each org — engineering first.
[05:42] Daniel: engineering highlights: rolled out continuous batching for two heavy routes, reduced token cost by about 12% in synthetic tests; ongoing work on autoscaler and the KV cache migration; hiring for two infra SREs is open (these are critical roles).
[06:08] Ethan: infra highlight: GPU packing experiments showed 10-15% better utilization on internal benchmarks; we still need to be careful on tail latency. kernel selection improvements landed in the canary and we're expanding.
[06:30] Lila: product highlight: we shipped prompt templates for support workflows which reduced average response cycles in a pilot with Customer Success. Q1 we hope to generalize templates and add routing policies.
[06:50] Jordan: GTM highlight: closed two dedicated deals, expanded proof-of-concept with a fintech customer into a 6-month pilot. churn metrics looking stable.
[07:05] Priya: finance highlight: Q4 close happening, auditor prep for some compliance add-ons; no surprises yet.
[07:18] Maya: People Ops: holiday schedule and a few changes to remote policy — they will send the full doc. please respect blackout dates for major releases.
[07:30] AMA segment: open mic.
[07:35] Audience (q): is there a target for cost-per-token reduction next year?
[07:40] Ethan: short answer — yes, target is mid-teens percent reduction on high-volume routes through batching, kernel, and quantization improvements by Q2. that's achievable but depends on model mix.
[07:55] Audience (q): what's the plan for SOC2/ISO audits?
[08:00] Priya: we're starting SOC2 Type II next quarter; security will post the timeline and the controls we'll be assessing.
[08:12] Audience (q): any update on onboarding enterprise console features?
[08:18] Lila: console 2.0 preview in Jan, it has per-model dashboards, rollout controls, and a new RBAC model. we'll demo to early partners.
[08:35] Audience (q): feedback — can we improve the length of release notes?
[08:40] Daniel: noted — we'll try summarized TL;DR lines at top of release notes and a quick changelog.
[08:50] Maya: closing thoughts — thank you to everyone for hard work in 2026, the plateau and maturity we see means it's time to be disciplined on costs and focused on the highest ROI product bets. we'll be conservative on hiring while we invest in reliability and product-market fit for dedicated/private.
[09:15] Maya: quick reminder — two weeks off for year-end holiday windows in some regions, check People Ops.
[09:30] Lila: final logistics: product will share the roadmap doc and intake form for pilots; reach out to product@ for prioritization.
[09:45] Jordan: sales will send the quarter wrap and competitive notes; please mark any leads in CRM.
[09:55] Maya: ok that's it. thanks everyone, short survey below the call, we appreciate feedback.
[10:05] End of recording.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors in product names and acronyms; speakers sometimes overlap. references: deck: //drive.company/redwood/q1-roadmap, security: //drive.company/redwood/security-soc2, billing memo: //drive.company/redwood/finance/q4-close
